newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriot clothing exports fall sharply in 95.
newsitem.headline: Cypriot clothing exports fall sharply in 95.

text.p: The Cyprus clothing industry on Wednesday appealled for government assistance to pull it out of a crisis that has seen exports plummet by 20 percent this year.

"The clothing industry is at the most crucial stage of its history and it is fighting for survival," said Sotiris Kallis, chairman of the Cyprus Clothing Manufacturers Association at the group's annual meeting.
Clothing industries annually top the list of Cypriot exports, absorbing around 23 percent of all exports.
In the first five months of this year, however, exports have fallen by 20 percent to 15.4 million pounds ($33.4 million) from 18.6 million pounds of exports in the first five months of 1995.

Earlier this year the government announced it would assist the manufacturing sector by offering low-interest long term loans for new technology. The clothing manufacturers association argues this is not enough.
Cypriot Commerce Minister Kyriakos Christofi, who addressed the gathering, said the competitiveness of the industry had slackened.
"Industrialists should put their efforts into finding new markets and the government has the means to assist them," he said.

Kallis said the sector was plagued with problems arising from increased trade union demands and what he described as a "pending demand with uncertain fate" for more government assistance to promote exports. Locally, Cypriot clothes are generally regarded as expensive compared to imported attire.
"The need to support local manufacturing is everybody's duty," said Kallis. ($1=0.46 pounds)
